AllowedTools.description:
Restricts this turn to a subset of the tools on offer.

`mode` of `auto` lets the model choose from that subset or answer
directly; `required` makes it call one of them. Every tool named here
must also be among the tools available to this request.

Annotation.description: An annotation attached to a span of output text.

ContentPart.description:
One piece of message content, discriminated by `type`.

The same set covers both directions: input text and attachments on the
way in, output text, refusals, and reasoning on the way out. A part you
send needs only the fields its own `type` defines.

oneOf.description: Text you are sending to the model.

Text the model produced.

`annotations` carries any citations for spans of this text.
`logprobs` carries per-token log probabilities; it is an empty array on
every response this surface produces today, because log probabilities
are never requested from a provider.
Plain text, where neither direction is implied.
A summary of the model's reasoning.
Reasoning text produced by the model.
The model declined to answer, and why.

An image you are sending to the model.

`image_url` accepts a URL or a data URL. `detail` asks for a
fidelity; omit it to let the model choose.
A file you are sending to the model, by URL or inline contents.
A video you are sending to the model.

ConversationItemList.description:
A page of a conversation's items.

`first_id` and `last_id` are always present, as empty strings on an empty
page. A client paginating with `after` uses `last_id`, and `has_more` is what
tells it whether to ask again.

data.description: The items, in the order you asked for.

first_id.description: The id of the first item on this page.

has_more.description: Whether more items exist after this page.

helpingio:unreadable.description:
Items on this page that are stored but could not be read. The other
items are returned in `data`. Omitted when every item was read.

last_id.description:
The id of the last item on this page; pass it as `after` for the next
page.

ConversationParam.description: The `conversation` a response belongs to: an id, or an object carrying one.

oneOf.description: An object carrying the conversation's opaque id.

ConversationResource.description:
A conversation.

OpenAI requires all four fields, so none of them is optional here and none
is skipped when empty. `metadata` in particular: a conversation with no
labels answers with `{}`, never with the field absent.

created_at.description: When the conversation was created, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

metadata.description: The customer's own labels on this conversation.

CreateConversationBody.description:
Create a conversation.

Both fields are optional: `POST /v1/conversations` with an empty body is a
valid call and gives you an empty conversation.

items.description:
Items to seed the conversation with, up to 20.

Seeded items become part of the conversation's context: the next
response on this conversation sees them.

metadata.description:
Labels to attach: up to 16 pairs, keys up to 64 characters, values up
to 512.

items.description: The items to add, up to 20 per call.

CreateResponseBody.description:
The body of a create-response request.

Fields you omit take their defaults, and fields this API does not
recognize are ignored rather than refused, so a newer client stays
compatible with an older server.

Every field of this body has one of four outcomes on this API: it is
applied, it is refused with an error that names it, it is accepted and not
applied, or it is advisory and the response reports what was applied rather
than what you sent. The generation settings are applied when the
model supports them, and refused with an error that names the model and
the field when it does not.

`truncation` IS applied: `disabled`, the default, refuses a turn that will
not fit the model's context window, and `auto` lets the oldest turns be
dropped so it fits.

The compatibility page says which outcome each field has, and its tables
are generated from the same classification the server refuses from.

background.description:
Runs the response in the background.

Not accepted today: `background: true` is refused. A non-streaming
request that outlives its wait window already returns the response
in progress for you to retrieve later, which covers the same need.

conversation.description:
The conversation this response belongs to.

Either the conversation's id as a string, or an object carrying it.
The conversation's items are the context for this response, and this
response's input and output are added to it when it completes.

Cannot be combined with `previous_response_id`: both name a
conversation, and a request that names two is refused rather than
resolved by precedence.

frequency_penalty.description:
Penalty applied in proportion to how often a token has appeared.

Applied when the model accepts it. When the model does not,
or the value is outside the range the model accepts, the request is
refused with an error that names the model and the field.
The response reports the value it was generated with, and 0 when no
penalty was applied.

helpingio:memory.description:
Turn memory on for the conversation this response starts.

Set on a conversation's first response. With `true`, the model keeps
facts about the person and reads them back on later turns. Later turns
keep what the first one chose: the same value again changes nothing,
and a different one is refused.

include.description: Extras to return that are omitted by default.

instructions.description:
Steering text for this turn only.

Applies to this request and is not inherited by later turns.

max_output_tokens.description:
Caps the tokens this response may produce.

The smallest accepted value is 16.

max_tool_calls.description:
Caps how many tool calls the model may make while generating this
response.

Counts every tool call, not only built-in tools, across every turn of
the response. Your organization's policy also limits how many calls one
turn may make. Calls past either limit are neither returned nor run,
and `helpingio:tool_calls_dropped` on the response says how many were
cut. The smallest accepted value is 1.

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach, echoed back on the response.

model.description: The model to run, either bare or as `provider/model`.

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Whether the model may request several tool calls at once.

Applied when the model accepts it. When the model does not,
or the value is outside the range the model accepts, the request is
refused with an error that names the model and the field.
The response reports the value it was generated with, and true when
none was set.

presence_penalty.description:
Penalty applied to tokens that have already appeared.

Applied when the model accepts it. When the model does not,
or the value is outside the range the model accepts, the request is
refused with an error that names the model and the field.
The response reports the value it was generated with, and 0 when no
penalty was applied.

previous_response_id.description:
Continues the conversation that produced this response id.

The API keeps the history, so a later turn sends only the new input
rather than replaying what came before.

prompt_cache_key.description:
A key that groups requests which share a prompt prefix.

Advisory. What this API does with it is on the compatibility page.

reasoning.description:
Reasoning settings.

Not accepted today: sending this is refused rather than ignored,
because a caller who sets it should not believe it was applied.

safety_identifier.description:
An opaque identifier for the end user this request is on behalf of,
used to detect abuse by one end user without restricting your whole
key.

Sent on the model calls this response makes for your request, where
the model's provider has a per-end-user field, as a keyed hash of your
value rather than the value itself. The response reports the value
you sent. A request that sends tool output keeps the value of the
request that asked for the tool call.

service_tier.description:
The service tier to run under.

Advisory. What this API does with it is on the compatibility page.

store.description:
Whether the response is stored so it can be retrieved later.

Defaults to true, and true is the only value this API accepts today:
`store: false` is refused rather than silently stored.

stream.description:
Streams the response as server-sent events instead of returning it
in one body.

stream_options.description: Options that apply only when `stream` is true.

temperature.description:
Sampling temperature.

Applied when the model accepts it. When the model does not,
or the value is outside the range the model accepts, the request is
refused with an error that names the model and the field.
When you omit it, the model's own default
applies. The response reports the temperature it was generated
with, and 1 when none was set.

text.description:
Settings for the response text, including a required output shape.

`format` sets the output shape: `json_schema` constrains the output
to the schema you supply, and must carry one. `verbosity` sets how
much detail to aim for. Each is applied when the model
accepts it, and refused with an error that names the model and the
field when it does not. The response reports the format and
verbosity it was generated under.

tool_choice.description: How the model should decide about calling those tools.

tools.description: The tools the model may call on this turn.

top_logprobs.description:
How many alternative tokens to report log probabilities for.

No current model returns log probabilities, so a request that sets
this is refused with an error that names the model and the field. The
response reports 0.

top_p.description:
Nucleus sampling cutoff.

Applied when the model accepts it. When the model does not,
or the value is outside the range the model accepts, the request is
refused with an error that names the model and the field.
When you omit it, the model's own default
applies. The response reports the value it was generated with, and
1 when none was set.

truncation.description:
What to do when the conversation no longer fits the model's context
window.

`disabled`, the default, refuses the request with a 400 and the code
`context_length_exceeded`: nothing is dropped behind your back.
`auto` lets the oldest turns be dropped so the request can proceed.

The size of a turn is estimated rather than tokenized, so the refusal
sits a little inside the model's real limit; the compatibility page
says what that means in practice.

user.description:
Deprecated in favor of `safety_identifier`.

When `safety_identifier` is absent, this value is used as it would
be: the end user this request is on behalf of. When both are sent,
`safety_identifier` is used. It does not group requests for caching.

DeletedConversationResource.description: The answer to a conversation delete.

id.description: The conversation's opaque id, echoed from the request.

ErrorPayload.description:
The body of a streaming `error` event.

Arrives in-band on the event stream when the response could not be
resolved. The stream ends after it.

FunctionCallField.description:
A tool call the model wants you to run.

Run it and send the result back as a function call output, quoting
`call_id`.

FunctionCallItem.description:
A tool call, as you replay it back on a later turn.

`call_id` is what ties this call to its output.

FunctionCallOutputField.description: A tool result, echoed back on the response.

FunctionCallOutputItem.description:
The result of a tool call, sent back so the model can continue.

`call_id` must be the one from the call this answers.

FunctionTool.description:
A function the model may call.

`parameters` is a JSON Schema describing the arguments. `strict` asks the
model to follow that schema exactly. When a tool is echoed back on a
response, `description`, `parameters`, and `strict` are always present,
and are `null` where you did not set them.

GatewayModel.description: One model you can call, identified as `provider/model`.

created.description: When the model became available, in Unix seconds.

helpingio:pricing.description:
What the model costs you now and what it is scheduled to cost, in
credits per million tokens. Omitted when the model has no price this
field can state exactly.

ImageDetail.description: How much fidelity to read an input image at.

Include.description:
Optional extras to return that are omitted by default.

Name one in `include` to have it present on the response. Every value the
Responses API defines is recognized. `reasoning.encrypted_content` is
returned; `message.output_text.logprobs` is refused on a model that does not
produce log probabilities; the other six are refused, because they name
tools or input this API does not offer.

IncompleteDetails.description: Why a response stopped before it was finished.

InputParam.description:
What to send the model: either a single string or a list of items.

A bare string is shorthand for one user message.

InputTokensDetails.description:
A breakdown of the input tokens counted.

Both fields are SUBSETS of `input_tokens`, not additions to it.

cache_write_tokens.description:
Input tokens written INTO the provider's prompt cache.

A provider that does not charge for a cache write reports `0` here.

cached_tokens.description: Input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache.

ItemField.description: One item of output, discriminated by `type`.

ItemOrder.description: How to order a page of items.

ItemParam.description:
One item of input.

Either a typed item or, with no `type` at all, a reference to an existing
item by id. An item carrying a `type` this API does not define is
rejected; it is never read as a reference.

ItemReference.description: A pointer to an item that already exists, by id.

ItemStatus.description:
How far along an output item is.

`in_progress` while the item is still being produced, `completed` when it
is final, and `incomplete` when the response stopped before the item was
finished.

LogProb.description:
The log probability of one output token.

This surface does not produce log probabilities yet: `top_logprobs` is
accepted and not applied, and `include: ["message.output_text.logprobs"]`
is accepted and not acted on, so the `logprobs` arrays that carry this
type are empty on every response today. They are arrays rather than nulls
because the schema requires an array, and an empty one is the honest
answer for "none were produced".

MessageContent.description:
Message content as either a plain string or a list of content parts.

A bare string is shorthand for a single text part, so the two forms are
interchangeable wherever this appears.

MessagePhase.description:
Whether an assistant message is the answer or commentary alongside it.

`final_answer` marks the message meant as the reply; `commentary` marks
narration produced on the way there.

ModelPricing.description: A model's prices, now and scheduled.

current.description:
The price per meter in force now, for a prompt of any length or, when
`tiers` is not empty, up to the first tier's threshold.

ends_at.description:
When `current` stops: after it, requests for the model are refused
until a new price is published. Absent when no end is scheduled.

scheduled.description: Prices already scheduled to replace `current`, earliest first.

tiers.description:
Prices for longer prompts: each applies to a whole request whose
prompt is above its threshold. Empty when the price does not depend on
prompt length.

OutputTokensDetails.description: A breakdown of the output tokens counted.

PriceTier.description: The prices of a request whose prompt is above `above_prompt_tokens`.

ReasoningConfig.description:
Reasoning settings.

On a response this reports the settings that applied. This API does not
accept it on a request: sending this field is refused rather than
ignored.

ReasoningEffort.description:
How much reasoning the model should spend before answering.

Higher settings trade latency and cost for more deliberation. `none`
disables reasoning where the model supports doing so.

ReasoningField.description:
Reasoning the model produced.

`encrypted_content` is present only when you asked for it in `include`.

ReasoningItemParam.description:
Reasoning from an earlier turn, replayed back.

`encrypted_content` is opaque: pass it back unchanged to carry reasoning
across turns.

ReasoningSummary.description: How much of the model's reasoning to summarize back to you, when a summary is produced at all.

ResponseConversation.description:
The conversation a response belongs to.

Its items are the context the response ran on, and the response's own
input and output are added to it.

ResponseError.description:
Why a response failed, carried on the response object itself.

A response that fails after it started is not an HTTP error: the request
succeeds and the response object carries `status: "failed"` and this.

helpingio:schema_source.description:
On `output_schema_mismatch` only: which schema the reply was checked
against, `text.format` (the request's) or `declared` (the output the
workflow declares). Absent on every other code.

ResponseFormat.description:
The shape the response text should take.

`text` is unconstrained prose, `json_object` asks for any JSON object,
and `json_schema` constrains the output to a schema you supply.

conversation.description:
The conversation this response belongs to.

Every response on this API belongs to one, whether you named a
conversation on the request or let the API make one for you, so
this is the id to hand to the Conversations API or to a later turn.

max_tool_calls.description:
The maximum number of tool calls this response was allowed to make.

The `max_tool_calls` sent with the request that started the turn, and
`null` when that request sent none. A request that sends tool output
keeps that value: a `max_tool_calls` sent with it is ignored.

metadata.description:
Whatever metadata you attached to the request, echoed back.

Always present, and `null` when you attached none.

service_tier.description: The service tier this response ran under.

status.description:
Where this response is in its lifecycle.

One of `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, `incomplete`,
or `cancelled`. `queued` and `in_progress` mean it is still running
and can be retrieved again later; the rest are terminal. Treat it as
an open string so a status added later does not break your client.

usage.description:
What this response consumed.

ABSENT while the response is still running, and present once it
settles. A response that is `queued` or `in_progress` has spent
nothing you can be billed for yet, so there is no figure to report,
and the field is left out rather than sent as `null`.

ResponseResource.description:
A response: one model turn, with everything it produced and the settings
it ran under.

The settings are echoed back as they were applied, which is not always
what you sent: values you omitted are filled in, and values capped by
your organization's policy are reported at the capped figure.

ends_at.description:
When these prices stop, as `ModelPricing::ends_at` states it for the
current price. Absent when no end follows them.

ServiceTier.description: The service tier a request asks for.

SpecificFunction.description: Names the function the model is being told to call.

SpecificToolChoice.description: Requires the model to call one named tool.

StreamOptions.description: Options that apply only when `stream` is true.

include_obfuscation.description:
Pads each streamed delta event with an `obfuscation` string so the
size of the event does not track the length of the text in it.

On unless you set it to false, which turns the padding off.

StreamingEvent.description:
The streaming event union. Variant order mirrors the response lifecycle:
creation, item lifecycle, content parts, deltas, terminals.

oneOf.description:
The stream failed and this is the last event you receive.

`code`, `message` and `param` are on the event itself, not nested:
read `message` for what went wrong and `code` to branch on it. The
codes are the same ones a non-streaming error carries.

code.description: Nullable in the schema; this surface always sets it.

param.description: Nullable in the schema; this surface has no parameter to name.

SystemMessageItem.description: A system or developer message: instructions rather than conversation.

Tool.description: A tool offered to the model, discriminated by `type`.

ToolChoice.description:
How the model should decide about calling tools.

Either a bare string (`none`, `auto`, or `required`) or an object that
names a specific tool or restricts the choice to a subset.

ToolChoiceValue.description:
The string form of `tool_choice`.

`auto` lets the model decide whether to call a tool, `required` makes it
call one, and `none` forbids tool calls for this turn.

TopLogProb.description: One alternative token the model considered, with its log probability.

Truncation.description:
What to do when a conversation no longer fits the model's context window.

`auto` lets the OLDEST turns be dropped so the request can proceed;
`disabled` fails the request instead of dropping anything, and is the
default (OpenAI's default too).

Oldest-first is the same end OpenAI documents dropping from: their own API
reference words `auto` as "dropping items from the beginning of the
conversation". The turn the caller just sent is never a candidate.

UnreadableItem.description: An item that is stored but could not be read.

id.description: The item's id. Retrieving it returns the same error.

UpdateConversationBody.description:
Replace a conversation's labels.

`metadata` is required: this operation exists to set it. Send `{}` to clear.

metadata.description: The labels to store, replacing whatever was there.

UrlCitation.description:
A cited web source, with the span of output text it supports.

`start_index` and `end_index` are offsets into that message's text.

Usage.description:
What this response consumed.

Present on terminal responses, including failed ones, so you can see what
a failed response cost.

Verbosity.description: How much detail to aim for in the response text.

api_key.description: An API key, presented as `Authorization: Bearer sk_...`.

info.description: The base URL is `https://api.helping.io`, and every path starts with `/v1`, so an OpenAI SDK takes `https://api.helping.io/v1` as its base URL.
info.title: helping.io API

post.description:
Send `input` and a `model`, or continue an existing conversation with
`previous_response_id`. The API keeps the history, so a later turn sends
only the new input.

Set `stream: true` to receive server-sent events instead of one body.
Without it the request waits a bounded time and, if the response is not
finished by then, returns it in progress for you to retrieve by id.

To answer a tool call, send its result as a `function_call_output` item
on the next turn, quoting the `call_id` from the call.

200.description: The response. With `stream: true` the body is a server-sent event stream instead, whose events carry this same object at its terminal (see the StreamingEvent schema). It keeps running, so retrieve it by that id for the result. A streamed response has no such bound.
